stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two maps. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1784, cartographer Ilse Varnhagen published a map of the Oder River delta.
• Varnhagen's map was engraved on copper plates and covered about 900 square kilometers.
• She gathered her measurements by walking the delta with a surveyor's chain.
• In 1791, cartographer Tomas Rečka published a map of the Morava floodplain.
• Rečka's map was printed from carved woodblocks and covered about 2,400 square kilometers.
• Rečka measured the floodplain on foot, pacing the land with a surveyor's chain.
choices: Varnhagen's map of the Oder delta was engraved on copper, whereas Rečka's map of the Morava floodplain was printed from woodblocks.
Both Varnhagen's 1784 map and Rečka's 1791 map were based on measurements taken on foot with a surveyor's chain.
Varnhagen's map covered about 900 square kilometers, less than half the area shown on Rečka's map of the Morava floodplain.
Varnhagen gathered the measurements for her 1784 map of the Oder River delta by walking the land with a surveyor's chain.
explanation: The two blocks of notes differ on printing method and area, but they share one feature: each cartographer measured the land on foot with a surveyor's chain. Choice B names both maps and uses 'both' to state that shared feature, so it does the job the goal asks for.

A.why: You picked an accurate detail, but 'whereas' marks a difference in printing method. The goal asked for a similarity, and this choice gives a contrast.

C.why: The arithmetic is right (900 is less than half of 2,400), but comparing sizes points out how the maps differ. It doesn't show anything they have in common.

D.why: This is the shared feature, but you only get it for Varnhagen. The sentence never says that Rečka worked the same way, so it doesn't establish a similarity.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the Velmora and Port Asher programs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A 2021 program in the rural district of Velmora sent mobile clinics to villages to offer measles vaccines.
• The Velmora program reached about 14,000 children in its first year.
• Its organizers trained local volunteers to explain the vaccine to parents.
• A 2022 program in the city of Port Asher set up measles vaccination booths inside public libraries.
• The Port Asher program reached about 6,500 children in its first year.
• Its organizers recruited neighborhood residents to answer parents' questions about the vaccine.
choices: The Velmora program brought measles vaccines to villages in mobile clinics, while the Port Asher program offered them in public libraries.
In its first year, the Velmora program reached about 14,000 children, more than twice as many as the Port Asher program reached.
Both the Velmora and Port Asher programs offered measles vaccines to children living in rural villages far from hospitals.
Both the Velmora and Port Asher programs relied on local community members to talk with parents about the measles vaccine.
explanation: The notes describe the two programs' communication in different words. Velmora used 'local volunteers' and Port Asher used 'neighborhood residents,' but in both cases community members explained the vaccine to parents. Choice D sees that the two notes describe the same thing and states it for both programs.

A.why: This falls for the subtype's trap. It accurately contrasts where the vaccines were given, and 'while' marks it as a difference, not a similarity.

B.why: The figures are accurate, but setting 14,000 against 6,500 shows how the programs differ in size. It doesn't show what they share.

C.why: Port Asher is a city whose program ran in public libraries, so 'rural villages' is true only of Velmora. You took a feature of one program and applied it to both.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the results of the two studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Agronomist Dalia Ferreira tested crimson clover as a winter cover crop on Iowa cornfields.
• The clover added nitrogen to the soil, reducing the fertilizer needed the next season.
• Clover-planted fields lost about 40 percent less topsoil to erosion than bare fields.
• Agronomist Kwame Oduya tested winter rye as a cover crop on Ohio soybean fields.
• The rye added no nitrogen but suppressed weeds the following spring.
• Rye-planted fields lost about 45 percent less topsoil to erosion than bare fields.
choices: In both studies, the fields planted with a winter cover crop lost at least 40 percent less topsoil to erosion than bare fields did.
Unlike winter rye, which suppressed weeds in spring, crimson clover added nitrogen to the soil and reduced the need for fertilizer.
Both crimson clover and winter rye added nitrogen to the soil, reducing the amount of fertilizer farmers needed the next season.
Ferreira found that planting crimson clover on Iowa cornfields reduced topsoil erosion by about 40 percent compared with bare fields.
explanation: The two studies found different secondary benefits, but both found less erosion: 40 percent for clover and 45 percent for rye. Choice A covers both studies with one accurate statement ('at least 40 percent') and uses 'in both studies' to make the shared result explicit.

B.why: This falls for the subtype's trap. It is a detailed and accurate sentence, but 'unlike' shows that it is about a difference between the crops.

C.why: The notes say the rye 'added no nitrogen.' You took a result from the clover study and applied it to both.

D.why: This states the shared result for Ferreira's study only. It never says that Oduya found the same thing, so no similarity is drawn.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two folktales. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• "The Salt Bride" is a folktale collected in coastal villages of northern Portugal.
• Its heroine is a fisherman's daughter who outwits a sea spirit.
• It was traditionally told by women as they mended fishing nets.
• "The Lantern Fox" is a folktale collected in mountain villages of central Japan.
• Its hero is a fox who guides lost travelers home through the snow.
• It was traditionally told by women as they wove cloth during the winter.
choices: "The Salt Bride" features a fisherman's daughter who outwits a sea spirit, whereas "The Lantern Fox" centers on a fox who guides travelers.
Both "The Salt Bride" and "The Lantern Fox" were collected in coastal villages where fishing was the main way of making a living.
Both "The Salt Bride" and "The Lantern Fox" were traditionally told by women while they worked, mending nets or weaving cloth.
"The Salt Bride," a folktale from northern Portugal, was traditionally told by women in coastal villages as they mended fishing nets.
explanation: The tales differ in where they come from and in their main characters. What they share is how they were told: by women doing handwork. Choice C names both tales and states that shared feature, keeping each tale's specific task (mending nets, weaving cloth) accurate.

A.why: You were drawn to the vivid plot details, but 'whereas' sets the main characters against each other. That is a contrast, not a similarity.

B.why: "The Lantern Fox" was collected in mountain villages, not coastal ones. You took a setting from one block of notes and applied it to both tales.

D.why: This gives the shared storytelling practice for "The Salt Bride" alone. Without "The Lantern Fox," there is nothing to be similar to.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the kora and the kantele. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The kora is a stringed instrument from West Africa.
• It has 21 strings, which the player plucks with the thumbs and index fingers.
• Its resonating body is made from a large calabash gourd.
• The kantele is a stringed instrument from Finland.
• Traditional kanteles have 5 strings, though modern concert versions can have up to 40.
• Players sound its strings by plucking them with the fingertips.
• Its body is often carved from a single piece of alder wood.
choices: The kora has 21 strings, whereas a traditional kantele has only 5, though concert versions of the kantele can have as many as 40.
Both the kora and the kantele have a resonating body that is carved by hand from a single piece of wood, often alder.
The kora of West Africa and the kantele of Finland are both played by plucking the instrument's strings with the fingers.
The kora, a stringed instrument from West Africa, is played by plucking its 21 strings with the thumbs and index fingers.
explanation: The notes describe the playing technique differently for each instrument ('thumbs and index fingers' and 'fingertips'), but both instruments are plucked with the fingers. Choice C names both instruments and joins them with one predicate introduced by 'both.'

A.why: This falls for the subtype's trap. Comparing string counts is accurate and detailed, but 'whereas' shows that it points out a difference.

B.why: The kora's body is a calabash gourd, not carved wood. You took a feature of the kantele and claimed it for both instruments.

D.why: This states the plucking technique only for the kora. It never says that the kantele is played the same way, so no similarity is established.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the outcomes of the two cities' plans. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Brenmouth's 2015 plan converted three downtown streets into pedestrian-only zones.
• Brenmouth's plan was approved after a two-year public comment period.
• Retail foot traffic downtown rose 18 percent within three years.
• Calder Falls's 2018 plan replaced a riverside highway with a public park.
• Calder Falls's plan was approved in a single council vote with little public input.
• Retail foot traffic near the river rose 22 percent within three years.
choices: Within three years, both Brenmouth and Calder Falls saw retail foot traffic in the redesigned area rise by roughly a fifth.
Brenmouth's plan was approved after two years of public comment, whereas Calder Falls's plan passed in a single council vote.
Both Brenmouth and Calder Falls approved their redesign plans only after a lengthy period of public comment from residents.
Brenmouth's 2015 plan, which made three downtown streets pedestrian-only, was followed by an 18 percent rise in retail foot traffic.
explanation: The goal asks about outcomes, so look at what happened after each plan. Foot traffic rose 18 percent in one city and 22 percent in the other, and both figures are roughly a fifth. Choice A does that conversion and uses 'both' to state the shared outcome for the two cities.

B.why: This falls for the subtype's trap. It accurately contrasts how the plans were approved, but that difference is about process, not outcomes, and 'whereas' marks a difference.

C.why: Calder Falls approved its plan in a single vote with little public input. You applied Brenmouth's process to both cities.

D.why: This gives the outcome for Brenmouth only. Without Calder Falls's result, the sentence describes one plan and doesn't draw a similarity.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Veyra-3b and Oskan-7c. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Veyra-3b is an exoplanet that orbits a red dwarf star every 11 days.
• It is about 1.3 times the diameter of Earth.
• Spectra of Veyra-3b's atmosphere reveal water vapor.
• Oskan-7c is an exoplanet that orbits a sun-like star every 290 days.
• It is about 2.6 times the diameter of Earth.
• Spectra of Oskan-7c's atmosphere show water vapor as well as methane.
choices: Veyra-3b completes an orbit of its red dwarf every 11 days, while Oskan-7c takes 290 days to circle its sun-like star.
At about 2.6 times the diameter of Earth, Oskan-7c is roughly twice as wide as the smaller exoplanet Veyra-3b.
Both Veyra-3b and Oskan-7c are roughly the size of Earth, and each of them orbits a cool red dwarf star.
Spectra of both Veyra-3b and Oskan-7c reveal water vapor in the atmospheres of these two distant exoplanets.
explanation: The planets differ in orbital period, host star, and size. The feature they share is water vapor in their atmospheres. Choice D names both planets and states that shared finding with 'both.' It correctly leaves out the methane, which only Oskan-7c has.

A.why: This falls for the subtype's trap. The orbital periods are accurate, but 'while' marks a difference between the planets.

B.why: The calculation is correct (2.6 is twice 1.3), but saying one planet is twice as wide as the other points out a difference in size, not a similarity.

C.why: Oskan-7c orbits a sun-like star, and at 2.6 Earth diameters it isn't roughly Earth-sized. You applied Veyra-3b's features to both planets.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the Arctic tern and the bar-tailed godwit. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Arctic tern breeds in Arctic and subarctic regions during the northern summer.
• It spends the northern winter in the seas near Antarctica.
• Its yearly round trip can exceed 70,000 kilometers, with frequent stops to feed at sea.
• Bar-tailed godwits that breed in Alaska spend the northern winter in New Zealand and eastern Australia.
• They make the southward journey in a single nonstop flight of about 11,000 kilometers.
choices: The Arctic tern stops often to feed during its migration, whereas the bar-tailed godwit flies south without stopping at all.
Both the Arctic tern and the Alaskan bar-tailed godwit travel to the Southern Hemisphere to spend the northern winter.
Both the Arctic tern and the bar-tailed godwit complete their southward migration in a single nonstop flight.
Each year, the Arctic tern's round-trip migration can exceed 70,000 kilometers, the longest yearly journey of any bird.
explanation: The terns winter near Antarctica and the godwits winter in New Zealand and Australia. The notes name different places, but all of them are in the Southern Hemisphere. Choice B sees that shared feature and states it for both species with 'both.'

A.why: This falls for the subtype's trap. It accurately contrasts the two birds' flight patterns, but 'whereas' shows that it describes a difference.

C.why: The notes say the Arctic tern makes 'frequent stops to feed.' You took the godwit's nonstop flight and applied it to both species.

D.why: The notes never say the tern's journey is the longest of any bird, and the sentence mentions only one species. It overstates the evidence and draws no similarity.
